procedure.step: Register the factory with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism; registration requires the factory to be located outside a free zone, a MoIAT industrial licence, and a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: Ensure the certificate application includes the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product; each item must qualify separately in its own right.
Log in to the ministry e-services portal.
Choose the Certificate of Origin for India service.
Upload the required documents: proof of factory registration, the commercial invoice, and for a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice.
Pay the certificate fee online. The fee is AED 50 (band: invoice value up to AED 100000).
Receive approval, or a return with comments to correct.

The certificate must be issued prior to, at, or within five working days of the date of exportation; it is valid for twelve months from the date of issue and covers only one import. A certificate may be issued retrospectively up to 12 months from the date of shipment, marked 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' in box 9.

Ship the goods directly from the UAE to India; transit through another country is allowed only under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar. If the invoice is issued by a third party, the exporter must indicate 'third-party invoicing'.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and must hold origin information, including which origin criterion is claimed; the importer keeps supporting documents for at least five years from filing and must answer a customs request within ten working days.
The exporter must keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least five years starting from the end of the calendar year of the certificate's issue.

caveats.note: '+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
A product that only undergoes the minimal operations listed in Art. 3.5.1 (a) to (q) does not originate, even if it meets its product-specific rule.
The agreement says box 8, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

Inference: a producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
Fee bands are in AED and apply to the invoice value in AED; no currency conversion is done by Mansha.
Inference: SWS is charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text found). Inference: anti-dumping and safeguard duties still apply (no exemption found).

That electronic certificates are accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system comes from CBIC Instruction 28/2022, which Mansha has read only through secondary reports (LiveLaw, taxmann), not the official text.
The issuing authority may apply risk management, including asking for detailed cost sheets and visiting the factory.

Cumulation is bilateral only: originating materials from India used in production in the UAE may be counted as originating. The last production process in the UAE must still go beyond the minimal operations.

Preference is given only to originating goods shipped directly from the UAE to India. Transit through another country is allowed only under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar. An invoice issued by a third party does not by itself cause the claim to be denied; the exporter must indicate 'third-party invoicing'.
